rationale: Ground truth is a near rubber-stamp (LGTM plus one off-diff ask to split out a VoxCPM2 fix) that neither candidate addresses, so recall is ~0 for both. Both independently converge on the same core mechanism and the same two actionable asks (tombstone comment explaining the missing seed, confirm the red NPU/AMD gates are pre-existing), which lends credibility to that shared core. X piles on extra claims — vLLM-version-specific sampler fallback behavior, a regression test, a warning-log suggestion — that add actionable volume but also unverifiable speculative depth for what is ultimately a trivial 2-line YAML deletion the human reviewer approved without comment. Y's report stays tightly scoped, tags each claim as validated/claim-verified/swept, and is proportionate to the actual change, making it the more reliably grounded of the two even though it covers less ground.
